questions.text: What does the chain rule let us compute?
options: The derivative of a composite function
The size of a gradient step

citations.quote: compute the derivative of a composite function by multiplying the derivatives of its parts

questions.text: Which rule does backpropagation apply layer by layer?

citations.quote: applies the chain rule layer by layer from the output back to the input

questions.text: After backpropagation has produced the gradients, which step uses them to change the weights?

citations.quote: used by gradient descent to update the weights

questions.text: In your own words, in which direction does gradient descent move the parameters?
questions.answer: In the direction of the negative gradient of the loss.

citations.quote: updates parameters in the direction of the negative gradient of the loss

questions.text: Why do networks use activation functions such as ReLU?
options: To reduce the number of weights

citations.quote: introduce non-linearity so that a network can represent more than a linear map

questions.text: Explain how backpropagation uses the chain rule.
options: It multiplies local derivatives layer by layer from the output back to the input
It averages the weights of all layers
It sorts the layers by size
It removes layers with small weights

citations.quote: applies the chain rule layer by layer from the output back to the input

questions.text: A parameter is 5.0, its gradient is 2.0 and the learning rate is 0.1. What is the parameter after one gradient descent step?

citations.quote: updates parameters in the direction of the negative gradient of the loss
The learning rate controls the size of each step
